title: Epic 2: Asset Pipeline
description: Build the scripts and processes that transform source media (MP4 video, PNG images) into the optimized WebP assets and generated TypeScript metadata modules the hero consumes at runtime. Three scripts: extract-frames.sh (ffmpeg → PNG at 15fps), optimise-assets.sh (cwebp → WebP at three tiers: thumb 480px, medium 960px, large 1920px), and emit-generated-hero-metadata.mjs (produces portalGeometry.ts and frameManifest.ts). The generated TS modules are the RUNTIME SOURCE OF TRUTH — the app imports them directly, never fetches JSON from /public (spec section 4.2). This eliminates metadata drift and extra network requests. Also covers preparing all static image assets (portal-composite, cosmos, arms, poster, trophy) to correct dimensions and quality.

title: 2.1: Create extract-frames.sh (ffmpeg → PNG at 15fps)
description: Script that takes source MP4 clips and extracts PNG frames at 15fps. 15fps is chosen because users control playback via scroll — they cannot perceive the difference between 15fps and 24fps at manual scroll speeds, and this saves 37% payload. The script should accept input path and output directory as arguments. It should normalize clips to exactly 4.000 seconds OR accept the true duration and let the manifest reflect the real extracted count (spec section 5.2). CRITICAL: do NOT hand-maintain TOTAL_FRAMES anywhere — the count comes from what ffmpeg actually extracts.

title: 2.2: Create optimise-assets.sh (cwebp → WebP at three tiers)
description: Script that converts extracted PNG frames to WebP at three tiers: thumb (480px wide), medium (960px wide), large (1920px wide). Also handles static images: portal-composite (1920px, q=80), portal-cosmos (1920px, q=80), arm-left/arm-right (1920px with alpha, q=80), trophy (long edge 1200px, q=85), stadium-poster (1920px, q=80). IMPORTANT for sparkle: must crush blacks so black pixels are exactly rgb(0,0,0) — any raised black level will tint the scene under mix-blend-mode: screen (spec section 5.3).

title: 2.3: Create emit-generated-hero-metadata.mjs
description: Node script that inspects the extracted/optimized frame directories and source assets, then emits two generated TypeScript modules: src/lib/hero/generated/portalGeometry.ts (artboard dimensions, hole center/diameter, arm bounding boxes as 'as const' export) and src/lib/hero/generated/frameManifest.ts (clip frame counts and available tiers as 'as const' export). These are the RUNTIME SOURCE OF TRUTH — the app imports them directly, NEVER fetches JSON from /public (spec section 4.2). This eliminates metadata drift and extra network requests. The script should read actual frame counts from the filesystem, not accept manual input.

title: 2.4: Prepare static image assets
description: Process the source images into their final WebP forms and place them in public/hero/: portal-composite.webp (shared opening still — used for LCP, static fallback, AND enhanced boot-still, spec section 2.2), portal-cosmos.webp (cosmos + portal ring + transparent hole, no arms), arm-left.webp (transparent WebP), arm-right.webp (transparent WebP), stadium-poster.webp (first frame of celebration clip — canvas fallback), trophy.webp. portal-composite must visually match the separated enhanced layers at rest so the BootStill→EnhancedHeroStage handoff is invisible.

title: 2.5: Extract & optimize celebration frames
description: Run extract-frames.sh on the celebration source video, then optimise-assets.sh to produce frames in public/hero/frames/celebration/{thumb,medium,large}/0001.webp through the last frame. Verify frame count matches what will be emitted in frameManifest.ts. Frame naming: zero-padded 4-digit (0001, 0002, ...). Target sizes: thumb ~3KB each, large ~12KB each.

title: 2.6: Extract & optimize sparkle frames (crush blacks)
description: Run extract-frames.sh on the sparkle source video, then optimise-assets.sh to produce frames in public/hero/frames/sparkle/{thumb,medium,large}/. CRITICAL: sparkle source must have TRUE BLACK background. Run black-level crush during preprocessing so black pixels are exactly rgb(0,0,0). Any raised black level will tint the scene when mix-blend-mode: screen is applied — the screen blend makes black invisible, so near-black becomes a visible tint. Verify by spot-checking pixel values in processed frames.

title: 2.7: Generate portalGeometry.ts
description: Run emit-generated-hero-metadata.mjs to produce src/lib/hero/generated/portalGeometry.ts. Output shape: export const PORTAL_GEOMETRY = { artboardWidth: 1920, artboardHeight: 1080, hole: { cx, cy, diameter }, leftArm: { x, y, width, height }, rightArm: { x, y, width, height } } as const. The hole center and diameter come from measuring the portal-cosmos source art. The arm bounding boxes come from the arm source images. These coordinates define the virtual 1920x1080 artboard that the portal composition is laid out on (spec section 13.1).

title: 2.8: Generate frameManifest.ts
description: Run emit-generated-hero-metadata.mjs to produce src/lib/hero/generated/frameManifest.ts. Output shape: export const FRAME_MANIFEST = { celebration: { count: N, tiers: ['thumb', 'medium', 'large'] }, sparkle: { count: N, tiers: ['thumb', 'medium', 'large'] } } as const. The count values MUST match the actual number of extracted frames — do NOT hardcode 60. The manifest is the runtime source of truth that frame-utils.ts and useFrameLoader.ts consume. Tier names MUST be exactly 'thumb', 'medium', 'large'.

title: Epic 7: Portal Phase (0.00–0.14)
description: Implement the portal zoom-through experience — the hero's opening act. PortalLayer.tsx composes the cosmos image and arm images within a virtual 1920x1080 artboard that is cover-fit into the viewport, using coordinates from generated portalGeometry.ts. Both cosmos wrapper and arms wrapper share the SAME transform-origin: the portal hole center converted to rendered artboard coordinates (spec section 13.2). Portal transforms (spec section 13.4): portalProgress = mapRangeClamped(scrollProgress, PORTAL_START, PORTAL_END, 0, 1). Cosmos: scale = 1 + easeInCubic(portalProgress) * (maxScale - 1), rotate = easeInCubic(portalProgress) * 1.5deg. Arms: same rotation but scale travel at 85% of cosmos (DELIBERATE compositional choice, NOT wrong parallax — arms linger as doorframe). MaxScale computed correctly: farthestCornerDistance / holeRadius * 1.05 (NOT imageWidth/holeDiameter). Ring pulse via CSS heartbeat animation (0.83s loop). Shooting star fires ONCE, 2s after enhancedReady (NOT raw mount), cancelled if scrollProgress > 0.06. Portal layers hidden after PORTAL_HIDE = 0.14, pulse/star stopped, will-change cleared.

title: 7.1: Implement PortalLayer.tsx — artboard composition
description: Create src/components/hero/PortalLayer.tsx (spec sections 13.1-13.2). Composes the portal scene within a virtual 1920x1080 artboard defined by PORTAL_GEOMETRY from generated/portalGeometry.ts. The artboard is COVER-FIT into the viewport (same cover-fit logic pattern as canvas). Inside the artboard: cosmos image fills it, left and right arm images are positioned using PORTAL_GEOMETRY.leftArm and PORTAL_GEOMETRY.rightArm coordinates. Both the cosmos wrapper and arms wrapper share the SAME transform-origin: the portal hole center (PORTAL_GEOMETRY.hole.cx, cy) converted into rendered artboard coordinates. This guarantees alignment at scale 1. Enhancement-only images (cosmos, arms) are loaded on the CLIENT only — not server-rendered (spec section 6.3). All layers: pointer-events: none, position: absolute, inset: 0. Portal cosmos at z-index 20, portal arms at z-index 21.

title: 7.2: Portal transforms — cosmos + arms scaling and rotation
description: Implement the portal zoom transforms (spec section 13.4). portalProgress = mapRangeClamped(scrollProgress, PHASES.PORTAL_START, PHASES.PORTAL_END, 0, 1). COSMOS transforms: scale = 1 + easeInCubic(portalProgress) * (maxScale - 1), rotate = easeInCubic(portalProgress) * 1.5 degrees. ARMS transforms: same rotation as cosmos. Scale travel = 85% of cosmos travel (arms scale multiplier is cosmos scale eased to 85% of the distance). This is INTENTIONAL — NOT wrong parallax. The arms lag behind the cosmos, creating a 'passing through a doorframe' sensation where the arms are the last visible part of the portal frame. Do NOT invert the scale ratio. The spec includes an explicit warning about this (Failure Mode 5). maxScale comes from computeMaxScale in math.ts. Apply transforms via CSS transform property on the cosmos and arms wrapper elements.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: WHY 85% ARM SCALE: This is the most counterintuitive design decision in the portal. Instinct says closer objects should scale faster (parallax). But this is NOT parallax — it's a compositional choice. The arms represent the portal frame (a doorway). As you 'fly through', the doorframe should be the LAST thing you see, lingering at the edges of your vision. If arms scaled faster, they'd vanish before the cosmos, which looks like the doorframe is flying away from you rather than you flying through it. The 85% value was chosen through visual iteration and is baked into the spec.

title: 7.3: Ring pulse CSS animation
description: Apply the 'heartbeat' CSS @keyframes animation (0.83s, infinite loop) to the portal ring element. The ring is part of the portal-cosmos.webp image — if it needs a separate animated element, use a CSS pseudo-element or overlay div positioned at the hole center. The pulse should be subtle and only run while the portal is visible (scrollProgress < PORTAL_HIDE). After PORTAL_HIDE, stop the animation and clear will-change if it was set. This is pure CSS animation, no JS needed beyond the visibility gate.

title: 7.4: Shooting star animation
description: Fire a single shooting star animation 2 seconds after enhancedReady becomes true (spec section 15.1). NOT 2 seconds after component mount — it must be tied to the enhancement lifecycle so it doesn't fire behind the boot-still or before the separated portal layers are visible. CANCEL the star if the user has already scrolled beyond scrollProgress 0.06 by the time the 2s timer fires. Use the 'shoot' CSS @keyframes animation (1.5s, once). This is a one-shot effect — gate with a ref, initialized from current scrollProgress on mount/pageshow. If the user arrives mid-page from bfcache with scrollProgress > 0.06, never show the star.

title: 7.5: Portal layer lifetime management
description: Implement portal layer cleanup at PORTAL_HIDE = 0.14 (spec section 13.5). When scrollProgress exceeds PORTAL_HIDE: (1) Stop ring pulse animation. (2) Cancel any pending shooting star timer. (3) Hide the portal layers (visibility: hidden or display: none). (4) Clear will-change if it was set dynamically (prevents GPU memory waste from layers that are no longer animated). When scrolling back up above PORTAL_HIDE, re-show the portal layers and resume pulse (but do NOT re-trigger shooting star — it's one-shot). All boundary values come from PHASES in constants.ts.

title: Epic 3: Core Library (lib/hero/)
description: Implement the five pure utility modules under src/lib/hero/ that every hook and component depends on. These are the mathematical and data foundations of the hero — they contain zero React, zero DOM, and are fully unit-testable. (1) constants.ts: the single PHASES object with all scroll boundaries, countdown target, scroll multipliers. (2) easing.ts: easeInCubic, easeOutCubic, bellCurve, clamp, mapRange, mapRangeClamped. (3) math.ts: drawCover (center-anchored cover-fit algorithm from spec section 10.4), portal artboard geometry calculations, maxScale computation (farthestCornerDistance/holeRadius * 1.05, NOT imageWidth/holeDiameter). (4) frame-utils.ts: celebration slow zone piecewise mapping (three-branch formula driven by FRAME_MANIFEST.celebration.count), sparkle linear mapping, draw key builder. (5) media.ts: tier selection by effectiveLongEdge (spec section 10.2), decode method abstraction (createImageBitmap primary, HTMLImageElement.decode fallback), AbortController + generation token management.

title: 3.1: Implement constants.ts — PHASES object + countdown + multipliers
description: Create src/lib/hero/constants.ts containing: (1) The PHASES object with ALL scroll boundaries exactly as defined in spec section 8: PORTAL_START(0.00), PORTAL_END(0.12), PORTAL_HIDE(0.14), VIGNETTE_START(0.00), VIGNETTE_PEAK(0.08), VIGNETTE_END(0.14), FLASH_START(0.10), FLASH_END(0.13), CELEBRATION_START(0.12), SLOW_ZONE_START(0.20), SLOW_ZONE_END(0.30), CELEBRATION_END(0.55), CELEBRATION_FADE_START(0.52), CELEBRATION_FADE_END(0.57), POSTER_HIDE(0.57), SPARKLE_PRESHOW(0.43), SPARKLE_START(0.45), SPARKLE_END(0.75), SPARKLE_HIDE(0.77), BLACKOUT_START(0.70), BLACKOUT_END(0.78), ANTICIPATION_START(0.78), ANTICIPATION_END(0.85), TROPHY_START(0.85), TROPHY_END(0.93), CTA_START(0.93), CTA_END(1.00) — all as const. (2) OPENING_MATCH_TARGET_ISO = '2026-06-11T19:00:00Z' (opening match kickoff, NOT ceremony). (3) COUNTDOWN_LABEL = 'Countdown to kickoff'. (4) Scroll multipliers: DESKTOP_MULTIPLIER = 4.5, COARSE_MULTIPLIER = 3.5. (5) SLOW_RATE = 0.5. ALL components import from here. NEVER hardcode boundary numbers in component files.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: ADDITION: The spec section 14.1 defines background fade values (black overlay 0.30→0.70) that are NOT in the PHASES object in section 8. To comply with Invariant 6 ('ALL phase boundaries come from constants.ts'), add BG_BLACK_FADE_START: 0.30 and BG_BLACK_FADE_END: 0.70 to the PHASES object. Without these, bead 11.1 (background layer) would have to hardcode 0.30 and 0.70, violating the single-source-of-truth principle.

title: 3.2: Implement easing.ts — math utilities
description: Create src/lib/hero/easing.ts with pure functions: (1) easeInCubic(t): t*t*t — used for portal zoom acceleration. (2) easeOutCubic(t): 1-(1-t)^3 — used for trophy entrance deceleration. (3) bellCurve(t): Math.sin(t * Math.PI) or 4*t*(1-t) — used for golden flash opacity. (4) clamp(value, min, max) — used everywhere, especially scrollProgress clamping. (5) mapRange(value, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax) — linear interpolation between ranges. (6) mapRangeClamped(value, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax) — mapRange but clamped to [outMin, outMax]. All functions are pure, zero side effects, fully unit-testable. easeInCubic(0) MUST equal 0, easeInCubic(1) MUST equal 1, must be monotonically increasing.

title: 3.3: Implement math.ts — cover-fit + portal geometry + maxScale
description: Create src/lib/hero/math.ts with: (1) drawCover(ctx, source, sourceWidth, sourceHeight, canvasWidth, canvasHeight) — the EXACT center-anchored cover-fit algorithm from spec section 10.4. Compares source and canvas aspect ratios, fits to dominant axis, centers and crops overflow. Poster object-position: 50% 50% MUST match this anchor. NEVER stretch via naive drawImage(0,0,w,h). (2) computePortalLayout(viewportWidth, viewportHeight, portalGeometry) — cover-fits the 1920x1080 artboard into the viewport, returns rendered positions for cosmos, arms, and hole center. (3) computeMaxScale(renderedHoleCenter, renderedHoleRadius, viewportWidth, viewportHeight) — computes distance from hole center to farthest viewport corner, returns (farthestCornerDistance / holeRadius) * 1.05. NOT imageWidth/holeDiameter — that old formula fails for off-center compositions (spec section 13.3).

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: COMMON MISTAKE: The maxScale calculation in previous spec versions used imageWidth / holeDiameter. This is WRONG for off-center portal compositions — the hole might not be centered in the image, so the scale needed to push the hole edge past the viewport corner is different. The correct formula from v3.1: (1) compute rendered hole center and hole radius at scale 1, (2) compute distance from hole center to the FARTHEST viewport corner (not nearest), (3) maxScale = (farthestCornerDistance / holeRadius) * 1.05. The 1.05 safety margin ensures no visible edge even with sub-pixel rounding.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: DEPENDENCY FIX: Removed dep on 2.7 (portalGeometry.ts). math.ts functions take portal geometry as PARAMETERS — computePortalLayout(viewportWidth, viewportHeight, portalGeometry). They define the type interface locally, they don't import the generated module. The actual import of PORTAL_GEOMETRY belongs in useHeroRuntime (4.2) and PortalLayer (7.1), which consume the generated values. This fix unblocks math.ts from the asset pipeline — it can now be built immediately after the directory structure exists.

title: 3.4: Implement frame-utils.ts — frame mapping + draw key
description: Create src/lib/hero/frame-utils.ts with: (1) getCelebrationFrameIndex(scrollProgress, totalFrames) — the THREE-BRANCH piecewise slow zone formula. Before slow zone (scrollProgress < SLOW_ZONE_START): linear mapping at full rate. During slow zone (SLOW_ZONE_START to SLOW_ZONE_END): advances at SLOW_RATE (0.5) of normal rate. After slow zone (> SLOW_ZONE_END): linear at full rate but offset by the accumulated slow-zone delta. totalFrames comes from FRAME_MANIFEST.celebration.count — NEVER hardcode it. Clamp scrollProgress to [CELEBRATION_START, CELEBRATION_END] before applying. From 0.55 to 0.57, hold last frame while fading out. (2) getSparkleFrameIndex(scrollProgress, totalFrames) — linear across [SPARKLE_START, SPARKLE_END], no slow zone. (3) buildDrawKey(frameIndex, activeTier, canvasWidth, canvasHeight, isVisible) — draw key for skip logic. Canvas MUST redraw when any component of this key changes, including tier upgrades without index change.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: THE SLOW ZONE FORMULA: The celebration frame mapping has three branches. Let progress = clamp(scrollProgress, CELEBRATION_START, CELEBRATION_END). Normalize to [0,1]. Then: (1) Before SLOW_ZONE_START: linear at rate 1.0. (2) During slow zone (SLOW_ZONE_START to SLOW_ZONE_END): rate drops to SLOW_RATE (0.5) — frames advance at half speed, lingering on the emotional peak. (3) After slow zone: back to rate 1.0, but offset by the accumulated delta from the slow zone. The total effective 'scroll distance' is compressed by the slow zone. Final frame index = floor(effectiveProgress * (totalFrames - 1)). totalFrames comes from FRAME_MANIFEST.celebration.count — NEVER hardcode 60.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: DEPENDENCY FIX: Removed dep on 2.8 (frameManifest.ts). getCelebrationFrameIndex(scrollProgress, totalFrames) takes totalFrames as a number parameter. getSparkleFrameIndex is the same. These are pure math functions that don't import FRAME_MANIFEST. The caller (useFrameLoader or the canvas component) passes FRAME_MANIFEST.celebration.count as the argument. The actual import of FRAME_MANIFEST belongs in useFrameLoader (4.3). This fix unblocks frame-utils.ts — it can now be built right after constants.ts and easing.ts.

title: 3.5: Implement media.ts — tier selection + decode abstraction
description: Create src/lib/hero/media.ts with: (1) getDesiredTier(viewportWidth, viewportHeight) — effectiveLongEdge = Math.max(w, h) * Math.min(devicePixelRatio || 1, 2). If <= 1100: 'medium'. Else: 'large'. Optional: if navigator.deviceMemory <= 4, prefer 'medium' on borderline. (2) getActiveTierLongEdge(tier) — large=1920, medium=960, thumb=480. Used for canvas backing store sizing (spec section 10.3). (3) computeCanvasScale(viewportWidth, viewportHeight, activeTierLongEdge) — Math.min(2, devicePixelRatio || 1, activeTierLongEdge / Math.max(w, h)). (4) decodeFrame(url, abortSignal) — primary: fetch + blob + createImageBitmap. Fallback: HTMLImageElement.decode + drawImage. (5) makeGenerationToken() — increments a counter, used to discard late fetch/decode results from stale tiers/windows.

title: Epic 10: Trophy Phase (0.85–1.00)
description: Implement TrophyReveal.tsx — the climactic finale. Trophy entrance: opacity 0→1, translateY 30px→0, ease-out across TROPHY_START (0.85) to TROPHY_END (0.93). Trophy lighting (spec section 14.6): NOT a viewport-wide spotlight overlay. Instead: render a dim base trophy, render a brighter trophy above it, mask the bright trophy with a radial gradient spotlight. Desktop: spotlight follows cursor via rAF-throttled pointer tracking. Coarse-pointer: centered spotlight with breathing CSS animation (spotlight-breathe 3s loop). Lens flare: one-shot CSS sweep (flare-sweep 1.5s) when trophy opacity FIRST crosses 0.8. CTA stack: primary <a> styled as button + secondary text <a>, padding-bottom: max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)). CTA MUST be inert until container opacity >= 0.8 (spec section 14.6) — prevents focus on invisible controls. CTA pulse: one-shot, 500ms delay after CTA opacity first reaches >= 0.8. Countdown: target 2026-06-11T19:00:00Z (opening match kickoff), Date.now(), update once/sec, clamp at zero, display 'XX days XX hours XX min XX sec', zero/negative → 'The World Cup has begun'. Countdown accessibility: visible timer aria-hidden, separate visually hidden status text updated at most once per minute.

title: 10.1: Implement TrophyReveal.tsx — trophy entrance animation
description: Create src/components/hero/TrophyReveal.tsx (spec section 14.6). Trophy entrance: opacity 0→1 and translateY 30px→0 with ease-out across TROPHY_START (0.85) to TROPHY_END (0.93). Use mapRangeClamped + easeOutCubic from easing.ts. Apply via CSS transform and opacity properties driven by scrollProgress CSS custom properties or direct style. z-index: 18. pointer-events: none on the trophy image itself — only the CTA stack below should accept interaction. The trophy image should be loaded lazily (not needed until scrollProgress > 0.50) per spec section 9.4.

title: 10.2: Trophy lighting — dim + bright + spotlight mask
description: Implement the trophy lighting system (spec section 14.6). NOT a viewport-wide spotlight overlay. Instead: (1) Render a DIM base trophy image (e.g., brightness filter or reduced opacity). (2) Render a BRIGHTER trophy image above it. (3) Mask the bright trophy with a radial gradient (CSS mask-image or clip-path) that acts as the spotlight circle. Desktop (fine pointer): spotlight position follows the mouse cursor, updated via rAF-throttled pointer tracking (not on every mousemove — batch through rAF). Coarse-pointer devices: spotlight is centered and uses the 'spotlight-breathe' CSS animation (3s loop) for a gentle pulsing size. This creates a premium, interactive feel without a heavy WebGL solution.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: TROPHY LIGHTING TECHNIQUE: The spec explicitly says NOT to use a viewport-wide spotlight overlay (which would dim everything including the background). Instead, the technique is: (1) dim base trophy (CSS filter brightness or opacity reduction), (2) exact same trophy image but bright (normal brightness), positioned identically on top, (3) bright trophy masked with a CSS mask-image radial-gradient that creates the spotlight circle. Only the area inside the 'spotlight' shows the bright trophy — everywhere else shows the dim version underneath. This is a standard compositing technique that avoids touching non-trophy pixels.

title: 10.3: Lens flare — one-shot sweep
description: Implement the lens flare effect (spec section 14.6). ONE-SHOT CSS animation (flare-sweep, 1.5s) that triggers when trophy opacity FIRST crosses 0.8. Gate with a ref initialized from current scrollProgress on mount/pageshow — if the user arrives mid-page with trophy already visible, do NOT fire the flare. The flare should be a visual sweep across the trophy area, implemented via CSS gradient animation or pseudo-element. pointer-events: none.

title: 10.4: CTA stack — primary + secondary links
description: Implement the CTA stack inside TrophyReveal (spec section 14.6). Primary CTA: semantic <a> styled as a button (gold background, hover gradient to Gold Light #E8D48B). Secondary CTA: semantic text <a> below the primary. Both must be real <a> tags (not <button>) since they navigate. Apply padding-bottom: max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) to avoid the CTA being obscured by mobile browser chrome / notch areas. Visible from CTA_START (0.93) to CTA_END (1.00). Opacity transition: fade in across that range.

title: 10.5: CTA inert management + pulse animation
description: Implement CTA interaction gating (Invariant 20, spec section 14.6). The CTA stack MUST have the 'inert' attribute until its container opacity >= 0.8. This prevents keyboard focus and pointer interaction from landing on invisible/barely-visible CTA controls. Remove 'inert' once the threshold is crossed. CTA pulse: one-shot 'cta-pulse' CSS animation (0.6s) that fires 500ms AFTER CTA opacity first reaches >= 0.8. Gate with a ref. The pulse draws the user's eye to the CTA at the moment it becomes fully interactive. Do NOT re-trigger the pulse on scroll-up.

title: 10.6: Countdown timer
description: Implement the countdown timer inside TrophyReveal (spec section 16). Target: OPENING_MATCH_TARGET_ISO = '2026-06-11T19:00:00Z' (opening match kickoff). Label: COUNTDOWN_LABEL = 'Countdown to kickoff'. Both imported from constants.ts. Behavior: use Date.now(), update once per second via setInterval, clamp remaining time at zero, clear interval on unmount. Display format: 'XX days XX hours XX min XX sec'. When remaining time <= 0: display 'The World Cup has begun'. Use a useEffect with cleanup for the interval.

title: 10.7: Countdown accessibility
description: Implement countdown accessibility (spec section 16.2). Do NOT expose a second-by-second live region to screen readers — this would be extremely annoying, announcing every second. Instead: (1) Visible timer element: aria-hidden='true'. (2) Separate visually hidden status text (sr-only) that is updated at MOST once per minute, or not live-announced at all. Use role='status' with aria-live='polite' if updating, but consider simply not making it a live region since the countdown is supplementary information, not critical.

title: Epic 13: Unit Tests
description: Comprehensive unit test suite for all pure library modules under src/lib/hero/. These are the MOST valuable tests in this project because the library functions are pure, deterministic, and contain the critical math that every visual layer depends on. A bug in easeInCubic, drawCover, or getCelebrationFrameIndex propagates to every component. Test runner: Vitest (fast, native TypeScript, ESM-compatible, integrates with Next.js). Every test file should have detailed logging of test inputs/outputs on failure so debugging is immediate. Test file naming: *.test.ts co-located with source. Coverage target: 100% branch coverage on all lib/hero/ modules.

title: 13.1: Test infrastructure — Vitest setup + test scripts
description: Set up Vitest for the Next.js 15 project. Install vitest, @testing-library/react (for component tests later), and configure vitest.config.ts to handle: TypeScript paths, 'as const' imports from generated modules, and ESM. Add to package.json: 'test': 'vitest run', 'test:watch': 'vitest', 'test:coverage': 'vitest run --coverage'. Configure console reporter with verbose output so every test case prints its name, inputs, and pass/fail on run. Add a custom reporter or use vitest's built-in verbose mode. Create a test/helpers/ directory with shared assertion utilities: expectCloseToZero(val), expectMonotonicallyIncreasing(fn, samples), expectWithinRange(val, min, max). These helpers should produce DETAILED failure messages showing the actual vs expected values and the input that produced them.

title: 13.2: Unit tests for easing.ts
description: Create src/lib/hero/easing.test.ts. Test every exported function exhaustively. EASING FUNCTIONS: (1) easeInCubic: boundary values (0→0, 1→1), midpoint (0.5→0.125), monotonically increasing (sample 100 points, verify each >= previous), negative inputs, inputs > 1. (2) easeOutCubic: same boundary + monotonicity checks, verify easeOutCubic(t) = 1 - easeInCubic(1-t) identity. (3) bellCurve: peaks at t=0.5, returns 0 at t=0 and t=1, symmetric (bellCurve(0.3) ≈ bellCurve(0.7)), always >= 0, max value ≈ 1.0. UTILITY FUNCTIONS: (4) clamp: clamp(5, 0, 10)=5, clamp(-1, 0, 10)=0, clamp(11, 0, 10)=10, clamp(NaN, 0, 10) (decide behavior and test), min > max edge case. (5) mapRange: mapRange(5, 0, 10, 0, 100)=50, boundary values, inverted ranges, zero-width input range (division by zero). (6) mapRangeClamped: same as mapRange but verify output is always within [outMin, outMax], including when input exceeds range. Log format on failure: 'FAIL: easeInCubic(0.5) expected 0.125, got {actual}. Input: 0.5'

title: 13.3: Unit tests for math.ts — drawCover + portal geometry + maxScale
description: Create src/lib/hero/math.test.ts. DRAW COVER: (1) Same aspect ratio: 16:9 source on 16:9 canvas → no cropping, draws full. (2) Wide source on narrow canvas (16:9 source on 9:16 canvas) → crops left/right, centers vertically. (3) Narrow source on wide canvas (9:16 source on 16:9 canvas) → crops top/bottom, centers horizontally. (4) Square source on non-square canvas → crops one axis. (5) Zero dimensions → handles gracefully. (6) Very large dimensions → no overflow. Verify: drawX + drawWidth >= canvasWidth OR drawY + drawHeight >= canvasHeight (cover guarantee). Verify: centering — abs(drawX) ≈ abs(canvasWidth - drawWidth - drawX). PORTAL LAYOUT: (7) 1920x1080 artboard cover-fit into 1920x1080 viewport → scale 1:1. (8) Cover-fit into 1080x1920 (portrait) → artboard scales up, crops top/bottom. (9) Cover-fit into 2560x1440 (ultrawide) → artboard scales, crops sides. MAX SCALE: (10) Centered hole → maxScale = (farthestCornerDist / holeRadius) * 1.05. (11) Off-center hole → farthest corner is farther, produces larger maxScale. (12) Very small hole → very large maxScale. Verify maxScale is ALWAYS > 1. Log format: 'drawCover(src=1920x1080, canvas=1080x1920): drawX={}, drawY={}, drawW={}, drawH={}'

title: 13.4: Unit tests for frame-utils.ts — slow zone + draw key
description: Create src/lib/hero/frame-utils.test.ts. CELEBRATION SLOW ZONE: (1) scrollProgress = CELEBRATION_START → frame index 0. (2) scrollProgress = CELEBRATION_END → frame index = totalFrames - 1 (last frame). (3) scrollProgress exactly at SLOW_ZONE_START → verify frame index (should be proportional to the pre-slow-zone scroll distance). (4) scrollProgress at midpoint of slow zone → frame should advance HALF as fast (compare frame delta across slow zone vs same scroll delta outside). (5) Monotonically non-decreasing: sweep scrollProgress from CELEBRATION_START to CELEBRATION_END in 1000 steps, verify frame index never decreases. (6) All frames used: sweep must hit every frame index from 0 to totalFrames-1. (7) totalFrames=1 edge case. (8) totalFrames=60 (typical). (9) During 0.55-0.57 (fade zone): should hold the last frame. SPARKLE LINEAR: (10) Linear mapping across [SPARKLE_START, SPARKLE_END]. (11) Boundary values: start→0, end→last frame. (12) Midpoint → middle frame. DRAW KEY: (13) Same inputs produce same key. (14) Different frame index → different key. (15) Different tier → different key (THIS catches the tier upgrade bug). (16) Different canvas size → different key. (17) Hidden → different key. Log: 'slowZone(progress={}, totalFrames={}): expected frame {}, got {}'

title: 13.5: Unit tests for media.ts — tier selection + canvas scale
description: Create src/lib/hero/media.test.ts. TIER SELECTION: (1) effectiveLongEdge = 1000 (mobile phone) → 'medium'. (2) effectiveLongEdge = 1500 (laptop) → 'large'. (3) effectiveLongEdge exactly 1100 (boundary) → 'medium' (<=1100). (4) effectiveLongEdge = 1101 → 'large'. (5) Test with various viewport × DPR combinations: 390×844 @3x → effectiveLongEdge = 844*2(capped) = 1688 → 'large'. 390×844 @1x → 844 → 'medium'. 1920×1080 @1x → 1920 → 'large'. ACTIVE TIER LONG EDGE: (6) 'large'→1920, 'medium'→960, 'thumb'→480. CANVAS SCALE: (7) scale = min(2, dpr, activeTierLongEdge/max(w,h)). (8) DPR 3 is capped at 2. (9) thumb tier on large viewport → scale < 1 (downscales to avoid exceeding thumb resolution). (10) large tier on small viewport → scale = dpr (or 2, whichever is less). Verify canvas dimensions are always Math.round'd integers. Log: 'getDesiredTier(viewport={}x{}, dpr={}): expected {}, got {}'

title: 13.6: Unit tests for constants.ts — PHASES validation
description: Create src/lib/hero/constants.test.ts. This is a SPEC CONFORMANCE test — it validates that the constants match the spec. (1) Verify every PHASES value matches the spec exactly: PORTAL_START=0, PORTAL_END=0.12, PORTAL_HIDE=0.14, etc. (2) Verify phase ordering invariants: PORTAL_START < PORTAL_END < PORTAL_HIDE, CELEBRATION_START < SLOW_ZONE_START < SLOW_ZONE_END < CELEBRATION_END < CELEBRATION_FADE_END, SPARKLE_PRESHOW < SPARKLE_START < SPARKLE_END < SPARKLE_HIDE, BLACKOUT_START < BLACKOUT_END, TROPHY_START < TROPHY_END, CTA_START < CTA_END. (3) Verify all values are in [0, 1]. (4) Verify OPENING_MATCH_TARGET_ISO is a valid ISO date string. (5) Verify SLOW_RATE is between 0 and 1 exclusive. (6) Verify countdown target is in the future (will start failing after the World Cup — that's OK, document it). Log: 'PHASES.{name}: expected {expected}, got {actual}'

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: ADDITION: Also verify BG_BLACK_FADE_START (0.30) and BG_BLACK_FADE_END (0.70) are in PHASES and have correct ordering: BG_BLACK_FADE_START < BG_BLACK_FADE_END, both within [0,1], and BG_BLACK_FADE_END <= BLACKOUT_START (the background fade-to-black should complete by the time the blackout overlay starts).

title: 13.7: Pipeline output validation — generated metadata + frame counts
description: Create scripts/validate-pipeline.test.mjs (or .ts if vitest can run it). Validates the OUTPUTS of the asset pipeline scripts to catch silent failures before they propagate to runtime. Tests: (1) FRAME COUNT CONSISTENCY: count files in public/hero/frames/celebration/{thumb,medium,large}/ — all three tiers must have the SAME count. Same for sparkle/. (2) MANIFEST ACCURACY: import FRAME_MANIFEST from generated/frameManifest.ts, verify celebration.count matches actual file count in celebration/thumb/, sparkle.count matches sparkle/thumb/. (3) TIER NAMES: verify FRAME_MANIFEST tiers arrays are exactly ['thumb', 'medium', 'large'] — no 'full', 'mobile', 'desktop'. (4) PORTAL GEOMETRY VALIDITY: import PORTAL_GEOMETRY from generated/portalGeometry.ts, verify artboardWidth=1920 and artboardHeight=1080, verify hole.cx and hole.cy are within artboard bounds, verify hole.diameter > 0, verify arm bounding boxes are within artboard bounds and don't overlap. (5) FILE NAMING: verify all frame files match /^\d{4}\.webp$/ pattern (zero-padded 4-digit). (6) SEQUENTIAL COMPLETENESS: verify no gaps in numbering (0001, 0002, ... 00XX with no missing numbers). (7) Generated TS IMPORTABILITY: dynamically import both generated modules and verify they don't throw. Log: 'VALIDATION: celebration has {N} frames across {tiers} tiers. frameManifest.celebration.count = {M}. Match: {yes/no}'

title: 13.8: Unit tests for countdown formatting logic
description: Extract or co-locate a formatCountdown(remainingMs: number): string function in TrophyReveal and test it. Tests: (1) Large time (90d, 5h, 30m, 15s) produces correct format 'XX days XX hours XX min XX sec'. (2) Zero remaining produces 'The World Cup has begun'. (3) Negative remaining produces 'The World Cup has begun' (clamped at zero per spec section 16). (4) Exactly 1 second remaining. (5) Very small remaining (500ms) — verify clamping. (6) Large value (365 days) — correct computation. If formatting is inlined and cannot be extracted, use component test with testing-library/react. Log format on failure: 'formatCountdown(input_ms): expected string, got actual_string'

title: Epic 1: Project Scaffolding
description: Initialize the Next.js 15 project with TypeScript strict mode, pnpm, Tailwind CSS v4, and the complete directory structure defined in spec section 20. This is the foundation everything else builds on. Includes layout.tsx with the critical beforeInteractive JS flag script that enables pre-paint mode selection (spec section 2.1), and globals.css with the CSS rules that select between static and enhanced branches without CLS. CRITICAL: The beforeInteractive script and mode-selection CSS must be correct from the start — they are the mechanism that prevents the layout shift that would occur if we rendered static first and swapped to enhanced after mount.

title: 1.1: Initialize Next.js 15 project with pnpm + TypeScript strict
description: Run 'pnpm create next-app@latest' with TypeScript, App Router, Tailwind CSS, ESLint. Verify tsconfig.json has strict: true. Verify package.json uses Next.js 15. Verify pnpm-lock.yaml exists (NOT package-lock.json or yarn.lock). Add to tsconfig: 'noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true' for extra safety. Node 22 LTS as engine target. This is the absolute foundation — nothing else can start until this compiles and 'pnpm dev' serves a blank page.

title: 1.2: Configure Tailwind CSS v4 with design tokens
description: Tailwind v4 uses CSS-first configuration (no tailwind.config.js). Set up globals.css with: @import 'tailwindcss'; design token custom properties for Navy (#1B2A4A), Gold (#C9A84C), Gold Light (#E8D48B), True Black (#000000); any font imports via next/font. The CSS file serves as the single theming source of truth. Verify 'pnpm build' still succeeds after configuration.

title: 1.3: Create public/hero/ directory structure
description: Create the complete public/hero/ tree: portal-composite.webp, portal-cosmos.webp, arm-left.webp, arm-right.webp, stadium-poster.webp, trophy.webp, frames/celebration/{thumb,medium,large}/, frames/sparkle/{thumb,medium,large}/. Tier names are EXACTLY thumb/medium/large — NEVER 'mobile', 'desktop', or 'full' (spec section 4.1). Directories can be created empty initially — assets will be placed by Epic 2. Purpose: establish the canonical asset paths that code will reference.

title: 1.4: Create src/ directory structure per spec section 20
description: Create the complete src/ tree: app/{layout.tsx, page.tsx, globals.css}, components/hero/{HeroSection.tsx, StaticHeroFallback.tsx, BootStill.tsx, EnhancedHeroStage.tsx, PortalLayer.tsx, FrameSequenceCanvas.tsx, SparkleOverlay.tsx, TrophyReveal.tsx, GoldenFlash.tsx, FilmGrain.tsx}, hooks/{useReducedMotion.ts, useFrameLoader.ts, useHeroRuntime.ts}, lib/hero/{constants.ts, easing.ts, math.ts, frame-utils.ts, media.ts, generated/{portalGeometry.ts, frameManifest.ts}}. Also scripts/{extract-frames.sh, optimise-assets.sh, emit-generated-hero-metadata.mjs}. Files can be stubs initially. CRITICAL: Do NOT create ANY directories or files not listed in the spec. No 'types/', 'utils/', 'config/', 'stores/', 'providers/', 'contexts/', 'services/'.

title: 1.5: layout.tsx with beforeInteractive JS flag script
description: In app/layout.tsx, add: <Script id='js-flag' strategy='beforeInteractive'>{`document.documentElement.dataset.js = 'true';`}</Script>. This tiny inline script runs BEFORE first paint and sets data-js='true' on <html>. Combined with the mode-selection CSS (task 1.6), it enables the correct branch (static vs enhanced) to be visible from the very first paint with ZERO layout shift. Without this, JS users would see the static branch flash before the enhanced branch replaces it. Also set up next/font loading, metadata, and viewport configuration here. This is the CLS prevention mechanism from spec section 2.1.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: CRITICAL CONTEXT: This tiny beforeInteractive script is the linchpin of the CLS prevention strategy. Without it, there is NO mechanism for CSS to know that JavaScript is available before first paint. The consequence would be: server renders both branches, CSS defaults to showing static branch, JS hydrates, React swaps to enhanced branch — a massive layout shift. With the script, CSS knows about JS before first paint and shows the correct branch immediately. The strategy='beforeInteractive' attribute is Next.js specific and ensures the script runs in <head> before any paint. Do NOT use 'afterInteractive' or 'lazyOnload' — those would defeat the purpose.

title: 1.6: globals.css mode-selection CSS + CSS animations
description: Add to globals.css the mode-selection rules that work with the beforeInteractive JS flag: .hero-static { display: block; } .hero-shell { display: none; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { html[data-js='true'] .hero-static { display: none; } html[data-js='true'] .hero-shell { display: block; } }. Also add all CSS @keyframes: heartbeat (0.83s, portal ring pulse), shoot (1.5s, shooting star), grain-shift (0.3s steps, film grain), flare-sweep (1.5s, lens flare), cta-pulse (0.6s), spotlight-breathe (3s, mobile trophy), anticipation-drift (4s). Also add hero-scroll, hero-stage, and layer positioning base rules from spec section 7.

title: Epic 14: E2E & Integration Tests
description: End-to-end and integration test suite using Playwright. These tests validate the hero as a COMPLETE EXPERIENCE in a real browser — scroll behavior, visual phase transitions, mode selection, accessibility, performance metrics, and edge cases. Unlike unit tests (which test pure math), these tests catch integration bugs: wrong z-index ordering, CSS not applying, scroll listener not firing, mode selection CSS failing, enhancedReady never resolving, CTA remaining inert when it shouldn't, etc. Every test should output detailed step-by-step logs showing what scroll position it's at, what it expects to see, and what it actually observes. Tests should take screenshots at key phase transitions for visual regression (stored in test/screenshots/ but gitignored). Playwright chosen over Cypress for: better multi-browser support (Safari via WebKit), better performance test APIs, native async/await.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: EPIC 14 vs EPIC 12: These automated tests should be runnable in CI without any manual intervention. They produce structured pass/fail output, screenshots at key frames, and detailed logs. They complement Epic 12 (manual QA on real devices) which catches perceptual issues automation misses.

title: 14.1: Playwright test infrastructure setup
description: Install and configure Playwright for the Next.js 15 project. Install @playwright/test. Create playwright.config.ts with: baseURL: http://localhost:3000, projects for chromium + webkit (mobile Safari coverage), webServer: { command: 'pnpm dev', port: 3000 }, timeout: 30s per test. Create test/e2e/ directory. Create test/e2e/helpers/scroll.ts with: scrollToProgress(page, progress) — programmatically scrolls to the exact scrollProgress value by calculating the pixel offset from the hero scroll container's measured position. This is the foundation of every E2E test — scrolling to a specific scrollProgress and asserting visual state. Also create test/e2e/helpers/logger.ts with a structured test logger: log.step(name), log.expect(description, expected, actual), log.screenshot(page, name). Create npm scripts: 'test:e2e': 'playwright test', 'test:e2e:ui': 'playwright test --ui', 'test:e2e:headed': 'playwright test --headed'.

title: 14.2: E2E — Full scroll-through phase validation
description: Create test/e2e/scroll-phases.spec.ts. The definitive test: scroll from 0 to 1 in small increments and verify every visual phase triggers at the correct scrollProgress. Steps: (1) Navigate to page, wait for hero to load. (2) Log viewport dimensions, scroll container height, computed scroll range. (3) Scroll to progress=0.00: verify portal cosmos visible, arms visible, static fallback hidden. (4) Scroll to 0.06: verify portal still zooming, ring pulse animation running. (5) Scroll to 0.11: verify golden flash has fired (opacity > 0 briefly), portal near max scale. (6) Scroll to 0.14: verify portal layers hidden. (7) Scroll to 0.15: verify celebration canvas visible, poster still visible behind. (8) Scroll to 0.25: verify slow zone — log frame index, verify it advances slower than at 0.15. (9) Scroll to 0.50: verify sparkle overlay visible (mix-blend-mode: screen). (10) Scroll to 0.55: verify celebration fading out. (11) Scroll to 0.75: verify blackout building. (12) Scroll to 0.80: verify blackout complete, anticipation particle visible. (13) Scroll to 0.90: verify trophy visible, opacity increasing. (14) Scroll to 0.95: verify CTA visible, not inert, interactable. (15) Scroll to 1.00: verify CTA fully visible, countdown ticking. (16) Scroll BACK to 0.50: verify one-shot effects (flash, flare, pulse) do NOT re-trigger. Screenshot at each step. Log every assertion with scroll position, expected state, actual state.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: ADDITION: At step (3) scrollProgress=0.00, also verify the background is navy (not black or white). At step (11) scrollProgress=0.75, verify the background is near-black (the BG overlay has fully faded in by 0.70). This confirms the two-layer background gradient is working. Check by sampling the hero root element's background-color or taking a screenshot pixel sample.

title: 14.3: E2E — Mode selection (JS / no-JS / reduced-motion)
description: Create test/e2e/mode-selection.spec.ts. Three test scenarios: (1) JS ENABLED + MOTION ALLOWED: navigate normally, verify .hero-shell is display:block, .hero-static is display:none, verify data-js='true' attribute on <html>, verify enhanced hero layers are present. (2) JS DISABLED: use Playwright's page.setJavaScriptEnabled(false), navigate, verify .hero-static is display:block and fully usable (portal-composite visible, stadium-poster visible, trophy visible, primary CTA clickable, secondary CTA clickable), verify .hero-shell is display:none. (3) REDUCED MOTION: use page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' }), navigate with JS enabled, verify .hero-static is display:block, verify .hero-shell is display:none even though data-js='true' is present (the @media query prevents the swap). Log each scenario's computed display values for both branches. Verify NO layout shift in any scenario by measuring CLS via PerformanceObserver.

title: 14.4: E2E — CLS measurement (zero layout shift)
description: Create test/e2e/cls.spec.ts. This test validates the ENTIRE CLS prevention strategy from spec section 2.1. (1) Inject a PerformanceObserver for 'layout-shift' entries before navigation. (2) Navigate to the page. (3) Wait for full load + enhancedReady (or static fallback). (4) Collect all layout shift entries. (5) Assert cumulative CLS = 0.000. (6) Log every layout shift entry if any exist: { value, sources, startTime, hadRecentInput }. (7) Also test: scroll through the entire hero — no layout shift during scroll. (8) Also test: the enhancedReady crossfade (BootStill → EnhancedHeroStage) produces no shift. If CLS > 0, the test should output the exact source elements and timestamps so we can trace which element shifted and why. This is the single most important performance test — CLS=0 is a non-negotiable invariant.

title: 14.5: E2E — bfcache restoration + mid-page landing
description: Create test/e2e/navigation.spec.ts. BFCACHE: (1) Navigate to hero page, scroll to progress=0.50 (past golden flash, into celebration). (2) Navigate to a different URL. (3) Go back (page.goBack()). (4) Verify: current scroll position is restored (~0.50), hero is in the correct visual state for 0.50 (celebration canvas showing, portal hidden, no golden flash re-trigger). (5) Scroll forward past trophy — verify lens flare fires (it hasn't been seen yet in this session). (6) Go back again — verify flare does NOT re-trigger. Log one-shot gate states at each step. MID-PAGE LANDING: (7) Navigate directly to page with a URL fragment or use page.evaluate to set scrollY. (8) Verify hero initializes correctly from the current position — correct visual layers showing, one-shot gates set appropriately (e.g., if landing at 0.90, golden flash gate should be 'already played'). Log scrollProgress, each one-shot gate, and visible layer states.

title: 14.6: E2E — Performance metrics (LCP + frame rate)
description: Create test/e2e/performance.spec.ts. LCP: (1) Navigate with Playwright's page.goto, (2) Collect LCP via PerformanceObserver, (3) Assert LCP < 2000ms (relaxed for CI — 1500ms target is for production 4G), (4) Assert LCP element is portal-composite.webp (log the element tag, src, and size). FRAME RATE: (5) Start a frame counter via page.evaluate (rAF loop counting frames), (6) Programmatically scroll through the hero over 3 seconds, (7) Stop counter, compute avg FPS, (8) Assert avg FPS > 50 (relaxed for CI headless — 60fps target is for real devices), (9) Log FPS per 500ms segment to identify specific scroll positions where drops occur. CANVAS DRAW CALLS: (10) Instrument CanvasRenderingContext2D.drawImage via page.evaluate to count calls, (11) Scroll past celebration (0.57), verify draw calls stop for celebration canvas, (12) Scroll past sparkle (0.77), verify draw calls stop for sparkle canvas. Log all metrics in structured format.

title: 14.7: E2E — Accessibility validation
description: Create test/e2e/accessibility.spec.ts. Use Playwright + axe-core (@axe-core/playwright) for automated accessibility audits. (1) Static mode: disable JS, navigate, run axe scan, assert 0 violations. Verify: <section> has accessible name, trophy img has alt text, CTAs are semantic <a> elements, heading structure is correct. (2) Enhanced mode: navigate normally, scroll to CTA (progress=0.95), run axe scan on the visible CTA region. (3) CTA inert test: scroll to progress=0.90 (CTA should be inert), verify CTA is not focusable via page.keyboard.press('Tab') — focus should NOT land on the CTA. Then scroll to 0.97 (CTA opacity >= 0.8), verify CTA IS focusable. (4) Inactive branch test: in enhanced mode, verify static branch has aria-hidden='true' and inert attribute. In static mode, verify enhanced shell has display:none. (5) Countdown: verify visible countdown has aria-hidden='true'. Log each check with: element selector, expected state, actual state.

title: 14.8: E2E — Runtime failure fallback
description: Create test/e2e/fallback.spec.ts. Validates Invariant 18: if the enhanced runtime fails, users see the static fallback. (1) Use page.route to intercept and abort the request for portal-cosmos.webp (critical enhancement asset), simulating a CDN failure. (2) Navigate to the page. (3) Wait for either enhancedReady or the fallback timeout. (4) Verify: static branch is visible, functional, CTAs clickable. The user should NOT be stuck in an empty 450dvh scroll container. (5) Variant: intercept ALL enhancement-only images — verify same graceful fallback. (6) Variant: use page.evaluate to throw an error inside EnhancedHeroStage on mount — verify error boundary catches and reveals static branch. Log the exact fallback path taken (timeout vs error boundary vs asset failure) and the final visible state.

title: 14.9: E2E — Viewport resize + orientation change
description: Create test/e2e/resize.spec.ts. Validates that the hero correctly recalculates layout variables on viewport changes (spec section 7.2). Tests: (1) ORIENTATION CHANGE: start in portrait (390x844), scroll to progress=0.30, then resize to landscape (844x390) via page.setViewportSize. Verify: --hero-vh updates to new viewport height, --hero-scroll-height recalculates (390*3.5 for coarse, 390*4.5 for fine), scrollProgress is correct at same pixel offset (it should change because scroll range changed), celebration frames still render (canvas resizes, backing store updates). (2) DESKTOP RESIZE: start at 1920x1080, scroll to 0.50, resize to 1280x720. Same verification — CSS vars update, scroll range recalculates, canvas re-sizes backing store. (3) Verify NO BLANK FRAME during resize — canvas must redraw with the new dimensions. (4) Verify the cover-fit recalculates correctly after resize (canvas content should be re-centered for the new aspect ratio). Log at each step: viewport dimensions, --hero-vh value, --hero-scroll-height value, scrollProgress, canvas.width/height.

title: Epic 6: Enhanced Shell & Scroll Architecture
description:
Build the enhanced mode structural scaffolding: HeroSection (root
), BootStill, EnhancedHeroStage, and the scroll/sticky architecture. HeroSection renders BOTH branches in a single
with an sr-only heading. BootStill shows portal-composite.webp inside the sticky stage and stays visible until enhancedReady — it IS the enhanced mode's first paint, so it must match the static branch's opening frame exactly (invisible handoff). EnhancedHeroStage is a client component that renders a LIGHTWEIGHT mount point on the server (no server-rendered enhancement-only tags per spec section 6.3) and only instantiates the layer stack on the client after enhanced mode is confirmed. The scroll architecture: hero-scroll (height via --hero-scroll-height CSS var, fallback 450dvh desktop / 350dvh coarse), hero-stage (position: sticky, top: 0, overflow: clip, isolation: isolate), all layers inside as position: absolute; inset: 0 (NEVER position: fixed, per spec section 7.4).

title: 6.1: Implement HeroSection.tsx — root section with both branches
description:
Create src/components/hero/HeroSection.tsx — the root component (spec section 6). Renders:

FIFA World Cup 2026 Tickets

. Both branches ALWAYS in the HTML. CSS selects which is visible. The sr-only heading provides document structure for accessibility. This component should be a server component — it just composes the two branches. The 'hero-root' element is where useHeroRuntime writes its CSS custom properties.

title: 6.2: Implement BootStill.tsx — enhanced mode boot still
description: Create src/components/hero/BootStill.tsx (spec section 6.2). Shows portal-composite.webp inside the sticky stage as the enhanced mode's opening visual. MUST be aria-hidden='true' (decorative in enhanced mode). Stays visible until enhancedReady becomes true (controlled via CSS class or style toggle from parent). The image should use the same visual framing as the separated enhanced layers at rest — when the crossfade happens from BootStill to EnhancedHeroStage, it must be INVISIBLE because both represent the exact same portal-composite frame. Use standard with appropriate sizing (not next/image if it complicates the sticky/absolute layout). This is a simple component — do not overcomplicate it.

title: 6.3: Implement EnhancedHeroStage.tsx — client component layer stack
description:
Create src/components/hero/EnhancedHeroStage.tsx (spec sections 6.3, 21.0). This is a 'use client' component. On the SERVER: render ONLY a lightweight mount point (
with the right classes). Do NOT server-render tags for portal-cosmos, arm-left, arm-right, or stadium-poster — otherwise reduced-motion/static users download images they never see (Invariant 13, Failure Mode 11). On the CLIENT: after enhanced mode is confirmed, instantiate the full layer stack: Background, Poster, FrameSequenceCanvas (celebration), SparkleOverlay, Blackout+Anticipation, TrophyReveal, PortalLayer, GoldenFlash, Vignette, FilmGrain. All layers positioned position: absolute; inset: 0 with z-index per Appendix B. Stay visually hidden (opacity: 0) until enhancedReady, then crossfade in as BootStill fades out. If runtime fails to initialize, fall back to making the static branch visible (Invariant 18).

title: 6.4: Scroll shell + sticky stage CSS structure
description: Implement the CSS for the scroll architecture (spec section 7): .hero-scroll { height: var(--hero-scroll-height, 450dvh); position: relative; } @media (pointer: coarse) { .hero-scroll { height: var(--hero-scroll-height, 350dvh); } } .hero-stage { position: sticky; top: 0; height: var(--hero-vh, 100dvh); overflow: clip; isolation: isolate; } All visual layers inside stage: { position: absolute; inset: 0; } The --hero-scroll-height and --hero-vh CSS variables are set at runtime by useHeroRuntime in pixels. The CSS fallbacks (450dvh, 350dvh, 100dvh) ensure the layout works even before JS sets the pixel values. If overflow: clip causes browser issues in QA, fall back to overflow: hidden.

title: 6.5: Wire enhancedReady gate — BootStill↔EnhancedHeroStage crossfade
description: Connect the enhancedReady signal from useHeroRuntime to control the BootStill→EnhancedHeroStage handoff (spec section 2.3). When enhancedReady transitions to true: (1) Fade BootStill opacity from 1 to 0. (2) Simultaneously fade the enhanced layer stack opacity from 0 to 1. (3) After crossfade, remove BootStill from the DOM or set display: none. The handoff must be INVISIBLE because both show the same portal-composite opening frame. Test by throttling network — BootStill should remain rock-solid until all 6 readiness conditions are met (cosmos decoded, arm-left decoded, arm-right decoded, stadium-poster decoded, portal geometry loaded, stage measured). Until ready: no decorative one-shot effects (shooting star, ring pulse visible but not started early).

title: 6.6: Runtime failure fallback to static branch
description: Implement Invariant 18: if the enhanced hero runtime fails to initialize (useHeroRuntime throws, EnhancedHeroStage errors, critical asset fetch fails permanently), the user MUST see the static fallback — NEVER be left in a non-animating 450dvh empty scroll shell. Implementation: wrap EnhancedHeroStage in an error boundary. If it catches, toggle the mode-selection classes so the static branch becomes visible and the enhanced shell is hidden. Also handle the case where enhancedReady never becomes true after a reasonable timeout (e.g., 10s) — fall back rather than leaving the user staring at an unmoving boot-still forever. This is the safety net for the entire enhanced experience.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: SAFETY NET: This is the last line of defense. Every other task assumes the happy path — assets load, canvas works, scroll events fire. This task handles what happens when they don't. Without this, a user on a flaky network or old browser gets stuck in a 450dvh tall empty scrollable page with nothing to see and no way to interact. The static fallback is always there in the HTML — we just need to make it visible again if the enhanced experience fails. Error boundary + timeout + class toggle. Simple but critical.

title: Epic 11: Decorative Layers
description: Implement the ambient visual layers that run throughout the experience. ALL decorative layers MUST have pointer-events: none — only the CTA stack accepts interaction. (1) Background: two stage-sized divs — navy base + black overlay fading in from 0.30→0.70. Two layers is cheaper than interpolating RGB every frame. (2) GoldenFlash.tsx: bell-curve opacity from FLASH_START (0.10) to FLASH_END (0.13), one-shot on first forward pass only (gated by ref, initialized from current scrollProgress on mount/pageshow). (3) Vignette: stage-sized radial-gradient overlay (NOT animated box-shadow), opacity ramp up 0.00→0.08, ramp down 0.08→0.14. (4) Blackout overlay: black div, opacity 0→1 from BLACKOUT_START (0.70) to BLACKOUT_END (0.78). (5) Anticipation particle: one subtle gold particle drifting during 0.78→0.85, ONLY when blackout is fully opaque AND trophy has not started. CSS anticipation-drift animation (4s loop). (6) FilmGrain.tsx: server component (zero client JS), SVG noise overlay, always on, subtle opacity, CSS-stepped jitter (grain-shift 0.3s steps loop), pointer-events: none.

title: 11.1: Background layer — navy base + black overlay fade
description: Implement the background layer inside EnhancedHeroStage (spec section 14.1). z-index: 0. Two stage-sized divs stacked: (1) Navy base (#1B2A4A, always visible). (2) Black overlay (#000000) that fades opacity from 0 to 1 across scrollProgress 0.30→0.70. Using two layers is cheaper and simpler than recomputing interpolated RGB values every frame via JS. The black overlay opacity is driven by CSS custom properties written by useHeroRuntime, or computed from scrollProgress. pointer-events: none on both.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: IMPORTANT: The fade range (0.30→0.70) mentioned in this bead's description MUST be imported from PHASES (as BG_BLACK_FADE_START and BG_BLACK_FADE_END), not hardcoded. Bead 3.1 (constants.ts) will include these values. This complies with AGENTS.md Invariant 6: no hardcoded scroll boundary numbers in components.

title: 11.2: Implement GoldenFlash.tsx — one-shot bell-curve flash
description: Create src/components/hero/GoldenFlash.tsx (spec section 14.9). z-index: 25. A full-stage gold-tinted overlay whose opacity follows a bell curve from FLASH_START (0.10) to FLASH_END (0.13). Use bellCurve from easing.ts. Peak opacity ~0.3 (subtle, not blinding). ONE-SHOT: only fires on the first forward pass. Gate with a ref (hasFlashPlayed). Initialize the ref from current scrollProgress on mount AND pageshow — if the user arrives mid-page with scrollProgress > 0.13, set hasFlashPlayed = true immediately so it never fires. On scroll-up past the flash zone, do NOT re-trigger. pointer-events: none.

title: 11.3: Vignette overlay
description: Implement the vignette layer inside EnhancedHeroStage (spec section 14.10). z-index: 28. A stage-sized radial-gradient overlay (NOT an animated inset box-shadow — gradients are cheaper). Use a transparent-to-black radial gradient. Opacity ramps UP from 0 at scrollProgress 0.00 to peak at 0.08, then ramps DOWN from 0.08 to 0 at 0.14 (matching VIGNETTE_START, VIGNETTE_PEAK, VIGNETTE_END from PHASES). The vignette creates a cinematic tunnel-vision effect during the portal zoom. pointer-events: none.

title: 11.4: Blackout overlay + anticipation particle
description: Implement two related effects (spec sections 14.5): (1) Blackout overlay: z-index 16, full-stage black div. Opacity 0 at BLACKOUT_START (0.70), opacity 1 at BLACKOUT_END (0.78). Linear interpolation via mapRangeClamped. This creates the dramatic fade-to-black before the trophy reveal. (2) Anticipation particle: during ANTICIPATION_START (0.78) to ANTICIPATION_END (0.85), show ONE subtle gold particle drifting, ONLY when blackout is fully opaque (opacity = 1) AND trophy has NOT started (scrollProgress < TROPHY_START). Use 'anticipation-drift' CSS animation (4s loop). The particle builds tension in the dark moment before the trophy. If the user scrolls past TROPHY_START, hide the particle. pointer-events: none on everything.

title: 11.5: Implement FilmGrain.tsx — server component SVG noise
description: Create src/components/hero/FilmGrain.tsx (spec section 14.11). This MUST be a server component (zero client JS) — it's pure CSS + SVG. z-index: 30 (topmost layer). Stage-sized decorative overlay, always visible, subtle opacity (~0.03-0.05). Uses an SVG <filter> with <feTurbulence> for procedural noise. CSS 'grain-shift' @keyframes animation (0.3s, steps, infinite loop) jitters the filter seed to create the film grain shimmer. MUST have pointer-events: none (it covers everything). The grain adds a subtle cinematic texture to the entire hero experience.

title: Epic 8: Celebration Phase (0.12–0.57)
description: Implement FrameSequenceCanvas.tsx — the reusable scroll-driven canvas renderer — and integrate it for the celebration clip. FrameSequenceCanvas is the most complex component: it chooses a frame index from scrollProgress, requests it from useFrameLoader, draws the nearest decoded frame if target is missing (NEVER blank), maintains a draw key (frame index + active tier + canvas width + canvas height + visibility), skips draws when hidden or key unchanged, handles resize safely, and sizes its backing store to the ACTIVE tier's long edge (NOT the desired tier — spec section 10.3). Uses drawCover from math.ts for center-anchored cover-fit (same as poster's object-position: 50% 50%). Celebration canvas visible from CELEBRATION_START (0.12), slow zone 0.20–0.30 (half-rate frame advance via piecewise formula in frame-utils.ts driven by FRAME_MANIFEST.celebration.count), fade opacity 1→0 during 0.52→0.57, hidden + stop drawing after 0.57. Poster layer always present at start, hidden after POSTER_HIDE (0.57), provides visual continuity when frames haven't decoded yet.

title: 8.1: Implement FrameSequenceCanvas.tsx — reusable scroll-driven canvas
description: Create src/components/hero/FrameSequenceCanvas.tsx — the most complex component (spec section 21.3). Props should include: clip name, phase boundaries (start/end for frame mapping), frame mapping function, scroll progress source. Responsibilities: (1) Choose frame index from scrollProgress using the provided mapping function. (2) Request target frame from useFrameLoader. (3) If target not decoded yet, draw the NEAREST available decoded frame (NEVER blank — Invariant 3). (4) Maintain a draw key: { frameIndex, activeTier, canvasWidth, canvasHeight, isVisible }. Skip draws when hidden or key unchanged. MUST redraw when tier upgrades even if index is same (Invariant 16). (5) Size canvas backing store to ACTIVE tier's long edge, NOT desired tier (Invariant 15, spec section 10.3): activeTierLongEdge = large?1920 : medium?960 : 480. scale = min(2, dpr, activeTierLongEdge/max(w,h)). canvas.width = round(viewportW * scale), canvas.height = round(viewportH * scale). (6) Use drawCover from math.ts for center-anchored cover-fit. (7) Handle resize safely (recalculate backing store, redraw). This component is REUSED by both celebration and sparkle — SparkleOverlay wraps it, does NOT duplicate it.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: ARCHITECTURAL NOTE: This is the single most important component in the hero. FrameSequenceCanvas is reused by BOTH the celebration (direct) and sparkle (via SparkleOverlay wrapper) phases. Getting this right means getting 60% of the visual experience right. The three hardest parts: (1) draw key logic — must include tier revisions so frames upgrading from thumb→large trigger redraws even when frame index is unchanged, (2) backing store sizing — must match ACTIVE tier, not desired tier, otherwise you get blurry upscaling or GPU memory waste, (3) never showing a blank frame — must always draw the nearest decoded frame when target is missing. If an agent builds this correctly, SparkleOverlay becomes trivial (just a CSS wrapper).

title: 8.2: Celebration canvas layer integration
description: Wire FrameSequenceCanvas into EnhancedHeroStage for the celebration clip. z-index: 11. Visible from CELEBRATION_START (0.12). Frame mapping: getCelebrationFrameIndex from frame-utils.ts (piecewise slow zone formula driven by FRAME_MANIFEST.celebration.count). Opacity: 1.0 while active. Fade from 1→0 during CELEBRATION_FADE_START (0.52) to CELEBRATION_FADE_END (0.57). After 0.57: set visibility: hidden AND stop drawing (canvas is expensive — don't draw to a hidden element). The slow zone between 0.20–0.30 makes frames advance at half rate, lingering on the emotional peak of the celebration. This pacing is deliberate — test that the slow zone actually feels like a 'pause' at the right scroll position.

title: 8.3: Poster layer
description: Implement the stadium-poster layer inside EnhancedHeroStage. z-index: 10 (under the celebration canvas). Always present from scroll start. Uses with object-fit: cover and object-position: 50% 50% (MUST match the canvas drawCover anchor — spec section 10.4). Purpose: provides visual continuity when celebration frames haven't decoded yet. The poster IS the first frame of the celebration clip, so when the canvas's first frame finally draws, it should be visually identical to the poster beneath it. Hidden after POSTER_HIDE (0.57) — by this point the celebration canvas has been rendering for a while and is fading out. pointer-events: none.

title: Epic 4: Hooks
description: Implement the three custom hooks that bridge the pure library code to React's lifecycle. (1) useReducedMotion: detects prefers-reduced-motion and gates the entire enhanced experience. (2) useHeroRuntime: the central nervous system — measures viewport, sets CSS variables (--hero-vh, --hero-scroll-height), owns the single passive scroll listener and single rAF tick, computes scrollProgress, writes CSS custom properties on the hero root (NOT React state — no re-renders on scroll), manages one-shot gate refs (initialized from current scrollProgress on mount AND pageshow for bfcache), exposes enhancedReady (true only when all 6 readiness conditions are met per spec section 2.3), responds to resize/orientationchange/visualViewport.resize/pageshow. (3) useFrameLoader: manages the entire frame lifecycle — proximity-based prefetch queue, HTTP cache warming (must NOT hoard Blobs in JS memory per spec section 12.1), ImageBitmap sliding window (20 large, 12 medium per active clip), .close() eviction, draw key revision tracking, cancellation via AbortController + generation tokens.

title: 4.1: Implement useReducedMotion.ts
description: Create src/hooks/useReducedMotion.ts. Detects prefers-reduced-motion: reduce via window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'). Returns a boolean. SSR-safe: defaults to false (assume motion allowed on server — CSS handles the actual pre-paint gate). Listens for change events so if a user toggles their system setting mid-session, the hero responds. This hook gates the ENTIRE enhanced experience — if it returns true, the enhanced shell must not activate, no scroll listeners, no frame preloading, no decorative motion (spec section 17). The CSS mode-selection rules (task 1.6) handle the pre-paint branch selection; this hook handles the post-mount behavior.

title: 4.2: Implement useHeroRuntime.ts
description: Create src/hooks/useHeroRuntime.ts — the central nervous system of the enhanced hero. Responsibilities (spec section 21.1): (1) Set --hero-vh from visualViewport?.height ?? window.innerHeight. (2) Set --hero-scroll-height from viewportH * (coarsePointer ? 3.5 : 4.5) in pixels. (3) Measure startY (scroll container document top) and endY (startY + scrollContainerHeight - viewportHeight). Recalculate on mount, pageshow, resize, scroll-shell size change (ResizeObserver on .hero-scroll). (4) Own ONE passive scroll listener. (5) Own ONE rAF tick that: measures scrollProgress = clamp((scrollY - startY) / (endY - startY), 0, 1), writes CSS custom properties on the hero root element, updates one-shot gate refs, schedules frame prefetch/decode work. NOT React state — CSS custom properties avoid re-render loops. (6) Initialize one-shot refs from current scrollProgress on mount AND pageshow (bfcache: if user returns mid-scroll, gates must be correct, not defaulted). (7) Respond to resize, orientationchange, visualViewport.resize, pageshow. (8) Expose enhancedReady: true only when ALL of: portal-cosmos decoded, arm-left decoded, arm-right decoded, stadium-poster decoded, portal geometry loaded, stage measured. (9) If runtime fails to initialize, signal failure so the hero can fall back to static branch (Invariant 18).

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: ARCHITECTURAL NOTE: useHeroRuntime is the central nervous system. Every other hook and component in the enhanced experience depends on it. Key design constraint: scrollProgress must be written as CSS CUSTOM PROPERTIES on the hero root element, NOT as React state. If you use React state, every scroll event triggers a re-render cascade through the entire component tree, which will destroy 60fps. CSS custom properties are read by components via getComputedStyle or CSS var() — no React re-render needed. One-shot gate refs must be initialized from CURRENT scrollProgress on mount AND on pageshow (bfcache restoration). If you only initialize on mount, a user who navigates away and presses back will get gates defaulted to false, causing effects to re-trigger at the wrong scroll position.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: DEPENDENCY ADDED: Now depends on 2.7 (portalGeometry.ts). useHeroRuntime imports PORTAL_GEOMETRY to check enhancedReady condition #5 ('portal geometry loaded from generated metadata'). The geometry data is also needed to compute the portal hole transform origin for the portal layer coordination. This is the correct location for this dependency — the hook imports the generated module, not the pure math functions.

title: 4.3: Implement useFrameLoader.ts
description: Create src/hooks/useFrameLoader.ts — manages the full frame lifecycle (spec sections 9.3, 12). Responsibilities: (1) Track frame availability by tier (which frames have thumb, which have desired full tier, which are in flight). (2) Warm HTTP cache in proximity-based priority order (spec section 9.3): current target frame → nearby frames → rest of thumb outward → current-window full-tier replacements → remaining full-tier outward. Use requestIdleCallback (fallback: small setTimeout). (3) MUST NOT keep every fetched frame as a JS Blob in memory — use browser HTTP cache (Invariant 21, spec section 12.1). (4) Manage decoded ImageBitmap sliding windows: 20 per active clip (large tier), 12 per active clip (medium tier). During clip overlap, both may be active. When clip becomes inactive, aggressively clear its window. (5) Evict ImageBitmaps via .close() immediately — not deref-and-wait-for-GC (Invariant 7). (6) Track draw key revisions so canvas redraws when a frame upgrades tier even if index is unchanged (Invariant 16). (7) Cancel stale fetch/decode work with AbortController + generation tokens — late results from old tiers/windows must be ignored. (8) Celebration thumb prefetch triggers at scrollProgress > 0.02 or idle. Sparkle thumb prefetch at > 0.30. Trophy lazy load at > 0.50 or idle.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: MEMORY MANAGEMENT: The frame loader has two caches that agents constantly confuse. The SOURCE CACHE is the browser HTTP cache — you warm it by fetching URLs, but you do NOT keep the response as a JS Blob. The DECODE CACHE is the sliding window of ImageBitmaps in JS memory. Only the decode cache is managed by this hook. When evicting from the decode cache, call .close() IMMEDIATELY — this releases GPU memory synchronously. If you just dereference the ImageBitmap, it stays in GPU memory until the JS garbage collector runs, which could be seconds or minutes later. On mobile with ~4GB total RAM, this difference matters enormously.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: DEPENDENCY ADDED: Now depends on 2.8 (frameManifest.ts). useFrameLoader imports FRAME_MANIFEST to know how many frames each clip has and which tiers are available. This drives the prefetch queue, the sliding window bounds, and the frame availability tracking. This is the correct location — the hook consumes the manifest, not the pure utility functions.

title: Epic 12: Performance, Accessibility & QA
description: Final validation pass before shipping. This epic covers all the measurable quality gates from the spec. (1) Lighthouse audit: LCP < 1.5s on 4G (portal-composite.webp with fetchPriority='high'), FCP < 1.0s, CLS = 0. (2) Bundle verification: Hero JS < 15KB gzipped, total hero payload < 2.5MB desktop / < 1.8MB mobile. (3) Memory profiling: verify sliding window budgets (large ~160MB/clip, medium ~24MB/clip, ~320MB worst overlap), verify no Blob hoarding in source cache, verify .close() on evicted ImageBitmaps. (4) Frame rate: 60fps scroll on M1 MacBook Air and mid-range Android, no canvas drawing when hidden. (5) Edge cases: bfcache restore (pageshow re-init + one-shot gate check), fast scrub (nearest decoded frame, recenter priority, don't walk sequentially), tier upgrade redraw (draw key catches it), hero runtime failure → static fallback (NEVER leave user in empty 450dvh shell). (6) Accessibility: inactive branch inert, CTA inert until opacity >= 0.8, sr-only heading, aria-hidden decorative layers, trophy image alt text, no second-by-second live region on countdown. (7) Mobile QA: iOS Safari, Android, coarse pointer, safe-area-inset-bottom.

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: EPIC 12 vs EPIC 14 DISTINCTION: Epic 12 is MANUAL quality assurance requiring real devices and human judgment — Lighthouse audits, DevTools memory profiling on physical Android/iOS devices, subjective frame rate evaluation, and manual accessibility verification. Epic 14 is AUTOMATED testing that runs in CI via Playwright and Vitest — programmatic scroll simulation, assertion-based phase validation, measurable CLS/LCP metrics, and axe-core accessibility scanning. Both are essential: automated tests catch regressions, manual QA catches visual/perceptual issues that automation can't detect (does the slow zone actually feel like a dramatic pause? does the trophy lighting look premium on OLED vs LCD?).

title: 12.1: Lighthouse audit — LCP, FCP, CLS targets
description: Run Lighthouse on the completed hero. Targets: LCP < 1.5s on simulated 4G (portal-composite.webp must be the LCP element with fetchPriority='high' and decoding='async'), FCP < 1.0s, CLS = 0 (verify pre-paint mode selection causes zero layout shift, verify enhancedReady handoff causes zero shift). If LCP is slow: check portal-composite.webp size, verify it's in initial HTML (not lazy-loaded), verify no render-blocking resources before it. If CLS > 0: check that both branches are in the HTML from server render, check mode-selection CSS is correct, check enhancedReady crossfade doesn't move layout.

title: 12.2: Memory profiling — sliding window + Blob hoarding
description: Profile GPU memory in Chrome DevTools. Verify: (1) Large tier: ~160MB per active clip, ~320MB worst overlap (both celebration and sparkle active). (2) Medium tier: ~24MB per clip, ~48MB worst overlap. (3) No Blob hoarding: open Performance Monitor, navigate the hero multiple times, verify JS heap does not grow unboundedly. The frame loader warms HTTP cache but must NOT retain Blobs in JS memory (Invariant 21). (4) ImageBitmap eviction: verify .close() is called when frames leave the sliding window — check via breakpoints or logging in useFrameLoader. Dereferencing without .close() leaks GPU memory until GC runs (Invariant 7). If memory exceeds budgets on medium-tier devices, reduce window sizes before changing visual design.

title: 12.3: Frame rate validation — 60fps on target devices
description: Profile frame rate on: (1) M1 MacBook Air (desktop baseline). (2) Mid-range Android (e.g., Pixel 6a, Samsung A53). Target: 60fps sustained scroll with no dropped frames. Check: no canvas drawing when hidden (celebration canvas must stop at 0.57, sparkle must stop at 0.77). Check: no React re-render loop on scroll (scrollProgress should be written as CSS custom properties, NOT React state). Check: rAF tick is not doing redundant work (draw key skip must be working). Check: will-change is cleared on portal layers after PORTAL_HIDE. If frame drops on mobile: check canvas backing store isn't oversized (should match active tier, not desired), check decode work isn't blocking main thread.

title: 12.4: Edge case testing
description: Test all edge cases from spec section 22: (1) bfcache restore (pageshow): navigate away, press back — hero must re-initialize from current scroll position, one-shot gates must be re-evaluated (don't re-fire flash if already past it). (2) Fast scrub: scroll rapidly through the hero — must see nearest decoded frame (never blank), decode priority recenters around target (doesn't walk sequentially). (3) Tier upgrade redraw: throttle network, scroll to celebration frames, watch as thumbs upgrade to medium/large — canvas must redraw even though frame index didn't change (draw key includes tier). (4) Hero runtime failure: deliberately break EnhancedHeroStage — must fall back to static branch (Invariant 18). (5) Mid-page landing: load the page with #fragment or deep scroll position — everything initializes correctly. (6) Scroll past hero: sticky stage releases, page content below is accessible. (7) Scroll back up: stage re-engages, one-shots don't re-fire.

comments.author: Victor
