comments.text: BFCACHE IS THE HARDEST EDGE CASE: When a user navigates away and presses back, the browser may restore the page from bfcache via a pageshow event. At this point: (1) The scroll position is wherever they left off — could be mid-celebration, mid-trophy, anywhere. (2) One-shot gate refs may have been initialized to default (false) if the component re-mounted, causing effects to incorrectly re-trigger. (3) The scroll listener and rAF may need to re-initialize. useHeroRuntime MUST handle pageshow by: re-measuring startY/endY, re-computing scrollProgress from current scrollY, and re-initializing all one-shot gate refs from the restored scrollProgress. Without this, coming back from bfcache produces a jarring flash of effects firing at the wrong time.

title: 12.5: Accessibility audit
description: Verify all accessibility requirements from spec section 18 and AGENTS.md invariants: (1) Inactive branch is inert + aria-hidden (Invariant 14). (2) CTA stack is inert until opacity >= 0.8 (Invariant 20). (3) sr-only heading exists and is associated via aria-labelledby. (4) All decorative layers have aria-hidden='true' (portal, canvases, flash, grain, vignette, sparkles, BootStill). (5) Trophy image alt text: 'FIFA World Cup 2026 Trophy'. (6) Primary and secondary CTAs are semantic <a> links. (7) Keyboard navigation: Tab should never land on invisible controls. (8) Countdown: visible timer is aria-hidden, not a second-by-second live region. (9) Enhanced canvases do NOT have role='img' (they are decorative). (10) Reduced motion: entire enhanced shell is inactive, static fallback is the only experience.

title: 12.6: Mobile QA — iOS Safari, Android, safe areas
description: Test on physical devices: (1) iOS Safari: verify scroll progress works with rubber-banding (clamp handles negative/over-1 values), verify portal-composite LCP, verify safe-area-inset-bottom on CTA. (2) Android Chrome: verify touch scroll feels smooth (passive scroll listener), verify frame loading on slower networks. (3) Coarse pointer detection: verify useHeroRuntime correctly detects pointer: coarse and uses 3.5x multiplier (shorter scroll distance) instead of 4.5x. (4) Trophy spotlight: verify centered breathing spotlight on touch devices (not cursor-following). (5) Viewport resize: verify orientation change recalculates --hero-vh and --hero-scroll-height correctly (spec section 7.2 — responds to resize, orientationchange, visualViewport.resize, pageshow). (6) safe-area-inset-bottom: verify CTA is not obscured by iOS home indicator or Android navigation bar.

title: 12.7: Bundle size + payload verification
description: Verify: (1) Hero JS bundle < 15KB gzipped. Check with 'pnpm build' output or next-bundle-analyzer. If over: identify what's heavy — likely the frame loader or canvas logic. No animation libraries should be in the tree (Invariant 1). (2) Total hero payload: < 2.5MB desktop, < 1.8MB mobile, spread across loading waves. Measure by: loading the page with Network tab open, scrolling through entire hero, recording total transferred for /hero/ assets. (3) portal-composite.webp should be the only critical blocking asset. Enhancement-only images (cosmos, arms, poster) should load after enhanced mode confirmed. Frame thumbs should load on scroll/idle. Trophy loads lazily. This loading waterfall is intentional — it ensures fast LCP while deferring non-critical bytes.

title: Epic 5: Static Branch
description: Build the no-JS / reduced-motion fallback experience. This is the branch that users see when JavaScript is unavailable or prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is set. It must be a complete, usable experience with no scroll animation — just a natural-flow stacked layout showing portal-composite, stadium-poster, trophy, primary CTA, and secondary CTA. The mode-selection CSS in globals.css (spec section 2.1) ensures this branch is shown by DEFAULT and the enhanced branch is hidden. The CSS rule @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { html[data-js='true'] ... } flips visibility BEFORE first paint. When static mode is active, the enhanced shell must be display: none (not just hidden — must not be in accessibility tree). When enhanced mode is active, the static branch gets aria-hidden='true' and inert.

title: 5.1: Implement StaticHeroFallback.tsx
description: Create src/components/hero/StaticHeroFallback.tsx — the complete no-JS / reduced-motion experience (spec section 6.1). Natural-flow stacked layout containing: (1) portal-composite.webp full-width (eager, fetchPriority='high' since it's the LCP candidate in static mode too). (2) stadium-poster.webp full-width (default priority). (3) Trophy block with alt='FIFA World Cup 2026 Trophy' (lazy loading). (4) Primary CTA: semantic styled as button. (5) Secondary CTA: semantic text . This branch must be fully usable with ZERO JavaScript. All images use next/image or standard with appropriate loading/priority attributes. No scroll listeners, no canvas, no animation hooks.

title: 5.2: Wire mode-selection CSS in globals.css
description: Ensure the mode-selection CSS from task 1.6 is integrated with the actual component class names from StaticHeroFallback and HeroSection. Verify: (1) Default state (no JS): .hero-static visible, .hero-shell hidden. (2) JS + no reduced motion: .hero-static hidden, .hero-shell visible. (3) JS + reduced motion: .hero-static visible, .hero-shell hidden (the @media prefers-reduced-motion gate prevents the swap even with data-js). Test by: disabling JS in DevTools, toggling reduced motion in system settings, checking both scenarios render correctly.

title: 5.3: Inactive branch inert/aria-hidden management
description: Implement the accessibility rules from spec section 6.4 and Invariant 14. When enhanced mode is active: static branch gets aria-hidden='true' and the 'inert' attribute (prevents focus from landing on static CTAs that are visually hidden). When static mode is active: enhanced shell is display: none via CSS (already removed from accessibility tree and tab order by virtue of not being rendered). Additionally, within the enhanced shell, the CTA stack inside TrophyReveal must be 'inert' until its container opacity >= 0.8 (Invariant 20). This prevents keyboard focus from landing on invisible CTA controls. Use the CSS pre-paint gate for the branch-level inert, and JavaScript for the CTA-level inert threshold.

title: Epic 9: Sparkle Phase (0.43–0.77)
description: Implement SparkleOverlay.tsx — a THIN wrapper around FrameSequenceCanvas that adds mix-blend-mode: screen via CSS. This is NOT a separate canvas implementation. SparkleOverlay renders FrameSequenceCanvas with sparkle-specific props (clip name, phase boundaries) and wraps it in a div with mix-blend-mode: screen. The stage's isolation: isolate ensures the screen blend doesn't leak outside the hero. ZERO canvas drawing code inside SparkleOverlay. Sparkle frames use LINEAR mapping across [SPARKLE_START, SPARKLE_END] — no slow zone. Visible from SPARKLE_PRESHOW (0.43), hidden after SPARKLE_HIDE (0.77), stop drawing. Sparkle source clips must have true black background (rgb(0,0,0)) — any raised black level tints the scene under screen blend.

title: 9.1: Implement SparkleOverlay.tsx — thin FrameSequenceCanvas wrapper
description: Create src/components/hero/SparkleOverlay.tsx (spec section 14.4, Invariant 5). This is a THIN WRAPPER — it renders FrameSequenceCanvas with sparkle-specific props and wraps the output in a div with mix-blend-mode: screen. ZERO canvas drawing code inside SparkleOverlay. The screen blend makes black pixels invisible and golden sparkle pixels composite additively. The parent stage has isolation: isolate so the blend doesn't leak outside the hero. z-index: 15. Visible from SPARKLE_PRESHOW (0.43). Hidden after SPARKLE_HIDE (0.77) — stop drawing. If you find yourself writing ctx.drawImage inside this component, you are doing it wrong. SparkleOverlay's ONLY job is:

comments.author: Victor
comments.text: CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: This component is a litmus test for whether the agent understands the architecture. The ENTIRE implementation should be roughly 20-30 lines — a div with mix-blend-mode: screen wrapping a FrameSequenceCanvas with sparkle-specific props. If the implementation exceeds 50 lines, something is wrong. If it contains canvas drawing code, ctx.drawImage, or ImageBitmap references, it is WRONG — those belong in FrameSequenceCanvas. This is Failure Mode 3 in AGENTS.md and the most common agent mistake observed on this codebase.

title: 9.2: Sparkle frame mapping — linear, no slow zone
description: Wire SparkleOverlay to use getSparkleFrameIndex from frame-utils.ts. Sparkle frames map LINEARLY across [SPARKLE_START (0.45), SPARKLE_END (0.75)] — no slow zone, no piecewise formula. Frame count from FRAME_MANIFEST.sparkle.count. Sparkle thumb prefetch triggers at scrollProgress > 0.30 (spec section 9.3). The visual result should be golden sparks flooding the frame as the celebration fades out, creating a seamless transition from celebration to blackout.
